title: Insecure Session Identifier Hashing (Low Entropy/Collision Risk)
pattern: Representing or validating session states using fast, non-cryptographic, low-entropy hashing algorithms.
why_bad: Non-cryptographic hashing algorithms are designed for speed, not collision resistance or unpredictability. Attackers can trivially compute collisions or brute-force user sessions, leading to privilege hijacking.
detection: The invocation of non-cryptographic hashes (`Fnv`, `MurmurHash`, `xxhash`) inside session generation methods.
fix: Represent session tokens using high-entropy secure hash algorithms (such as `SHA-256` or `SHA-3`) with cryptographically secure salts.
source: `Heather Adkins et al. - Building Secure and Reliable Systems (2020)`, Ch 18, p. 434.
